title: Refrigerator Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan motor in the freezer compartment is not running or reporting incorrect speed.
fullDescription:
The rF error on LG freezers indicates a fault with the evaporator fan motor responsible for circulating cold air inside the freezer compartment. The control board monitors fan RPM via a feedback wire and triggers this code when the fan fails to reach the expected speed or stalls.

Common root causes include ice buildup blocking the fan blade, a failed fan motor, a disconnected wiring harness, or a main PCB that cannot read the RPM signal. The freezer will typically begin to warm up within hours if the fan does not recover.

Thorough inspection usually involves removing the rear freezer panel to access the fan assembly, clearing any frost, and verifying the motor spins freely by hand.

causes.cause: Ice buildup blocking the fan blade
Loose or damaged wiring harness to the fan

fixSteps.title: Unplug freezer
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power at the outlet before any internal work.

fixSteps.title: Remove rear panel
fixSteps.instruction: Take out food and shelves, then remove the screws securing the rear evaporator cover.

fixSteps.title: Defrost fan area
fixSteps.instruction: Use a hair dryer on low or let the unit sit open to melt any ice around the fan blades.

fixSteps.title: Test fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Spin blade by hand; if stiff or noisy, replace the fan motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the fan runs but the code persists, indicating a main board fault.

faq.q: Can I keep using the freezer with rF?
faq.a: No, food will thaw. Transfer items to another freezer until fixed.
Only if the root cause was ice; if the defrost heater is failing it will return.

title: Defrost Heater Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The defrost cycle did not complete within the expected timeframe.
fullDescription:
The dH error indicates the freezer's automatic defrost cycle ran too long or did not raise the evaporator temperature as expected. LG control boards abort the defrost cycle and display dH when the bimetal thermostat or defrost sensor fails to signal completion.

Common causes include an open defrost heater, a failed defrost thermistor, or a stuck bimetal. Left unaddressed, frost accumulates on the evaporator coil and airflow drops, causing warm compartments.

Repair typically requires checking the heater resistance and thermistor readings with a multimeter after accessing the evaporator behind the rear freezer panel.

causes.cause: Main control board defrost circuit failure

fixSteps.title: Access evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel screws and gently pull cover off.

fixSteps.title: Manually defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Allow evaporator to thaw completely, 2-4 hours.

fixSteps.title: Test components
fixSteps.instruction: Measure defrost heater (typically 20-40 ohms) and thermistor resistance at room temperature.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you're not comfortable testing electrical components with a multimeter.

faq.q: Will manual defrost clear the code?
faq.a: Temporarily, but it will return until the faulty part is replaced.

faq.q: What resistance should the heater read?
faq.a: Most LG defrost heaters read between 20 and 40 ohms; open (OL) means it's failed.

title: Condenser Fan Motor Failure
shortDescription: The condenser fan motor is not running at the expected RPM.
fullDescription:
The CF error indicates the condenser fan, located near the compressor at the rear bottom of the freezer, is not spinning correctly. This fan cools the condenser coils and compressor during operation.

Causes range from dust-clogged blades and bearing failure to a damaged motor or disconnected harness. If not corrected, the compressor may overheat and shut down on thermal overload, causing warm temperatures.

Accessing the condenser fan usually requires removing the rear lower access panel of the freezer.

causes.cause: Dust and debris blocking the fan
Worn bearings in the fan motor

fixSteps.title: Unplug unit
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and pull freezer away from wall.

fixSteps.title: Remove back panel
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew lower rear access panel to expose compressor area.

fixSteps.title: Clean and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust from fan and condenser coils, then spin blade by hand to check for binding.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If blade is stiff or motor buzzes without spinning, replace the condenser fan motor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the motor is fine but the code persists, suggesting a board or wiring fault.

faq.q: Can I just clean the fan?
faq.a: Yes, if dust was the cause; otherwise the motor likely needs replacement.

faq.q: How often should I vacuum the condenser?
faq.a: Every 6-12 months to prevent recurrence.

title: Freezer Fan Malfunction
shortDescription: The internal freezer circulation fan is not operating correctly.
fullDescription:
FF on an LG freezer indicates that the internal circulation fan (sometimes called the freezer fan) has stopped or is running too slowly. This is usually the evaporator fan in a dedicated freezer or a secondary circulation fan in larger units.

Typical causes include ice on the blade, a wiring problem, or a failed motor. The freezer can tolerate brief fan outages but will warm up within a few hours if not addressed.

Diagnosis involves visually inspecting the fan, testing the motor with a multimeter, and ensuring the defrost system is working so ice does not recur.

causes.cause: Ice on fan blade or housing

fixSteps.title: Open and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel to view the fan.

fixSteps.title: Clear ice
fixSteps.instruction: Defrost any buildup and verify blade spins freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If motor is seized or non-responsive, install a new fan motor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you've replaced the fan and the error returns quickly.

faq.q: Is FF the same as rF?
faq.a: They're similar; FF typically refers to a secondary or compartment-specific fan.

faq.q: Can I ignore the code briefly?
faq.a: Only if you move food; contents will thaw within hours.

title: Extended Defrost Error
shortDescription: Defrost cycle exceeded maximum duration; heater or sensor likely at fault.
fullDescription:
Er DH is the verbose form of the dH code and indicates that the defrost heater ran beyond the safety time limit (typically 80 minutes) without raising the evaporator temperature sufficiently. The control board shuts the cycle down to prevent damage.

Root causes almost always involve the defrost heater itself or the defrost thermistor used to monitor evaporator temperature. A failing bimetal can also cause false timeouts.

Repair requires electrical testing of the heater circuit and thermistor, both accessible after removing the freezer rear panel.

fixSteps.title: Empty and access evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove food and the rear freezer panel.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; expect 20-40 ohms. Open circuit means replace.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare thermistor resistance to LG spec chart at known temperature.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for board-level diagnostics if heater and thermistor test good.
videoSearchQuery: LG freezer Er DH error fix

faq.q: Is Er DH different from dH?
faq.a: Same root fault; Er DH is shown on newer firmware versions.

faq.q: Can I bypass the defrost heater?
faq.a: No, that will damage the evaporator and void any warranty.

title: Linear Compressor Fault
shortDescription: Communication or operating error between the inverter board and linear compressor.
fullDescription:
The Er LC code appears on LG freezers equipped with the inverter linear compressor. The inverter board reports that the compressor is not starting, not reaching the required frequency, or that communication with the main PCB has failed.

Common causes include a failed inverter board (PCB mounted on top of the compressor), wiring or connector problems, or the compressor itself being defective. Many LG linear compressors are covered under a 10-year warranty so check coverage first.

Repair typically starts with the inverter board since it fails more frequently than the compressor itself.

fixSteps.title: Check warranty
fixSteps.instruction: Verify if the compressor is within its 10-year warranty using the serial number on LG's site.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes then restore power; some Er LC events clear.

fixSteps.title: Inspect inverter board
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug freezer, access rear, inspect inverter board for burns or swollen capacitors.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter board
fixSteps.instruction: If damaged or code persists after swap, replace inverter board first; compressor replacement is a pro job.

whenToCallPro: Compressor replacement requires EPA certification for sealed-system work; always hire a pro.
videoSearchQuery: LG freezer Er LC error fix

faq.q: Is the compressor covered by warranty?
faq.a: LG linear compressors typically carry a 10-year parts warranty.

faq.q: Should I replace inverter or compressor first?
faq.a: Inverter board; it's cheaper and the more common failure.

title: Evaporator Fan Circuit Error
shortDescription: Extended evaporator fan fault with board-reported RPM mismatch.
fullDescription:
Er rF is the detailed version of the rF error and indicates a persistent fault with the evaporator fan motor. The control board has logged repeated RPM feedback errors and the fan is either stalled, under-speed, or disconnected entirely.

The troubleshooting flow is similar to rF: inspect for ice, test motor continuity, and check harness continuity. If those all test good, the main PCB fan driver circuit is the likely culprit.

This code usually appears after an initial rF warning is ignored for several cycles.

fixSteps.title: Access fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear evaporator cover inside freezer.

fixSteps.title: Defrost and test
fixSteps.instruction: Clear ice and spin blade; measure motor resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the fan motor; if code persists, escalate to a technician for board diagnosis.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the motor and wiring test good but the code returns.
videoSearchQuery: LG freezer Er rF error fix

faq.q: Why did rF escalate to Er rF?
faq.a: The board marked the fault persistent across multiple cycles.
Only temporarily; replace the motor if it's physically damaged.

title: Freezer Fan Error (Extended)
fullDescription:
Er FF indicates the freezer circulation fan has failed repeatedly and the control board has logged the fault as persistent. It is the long-form companion to the FF code.

Causes mirror FF: icing, motor failure, or wiring issues. Since the error is persistent, plan on replacing the motor rather than attempting a simple defrost.

If the defrost system is also failing, clearing Er FF without fixing defrost will likely lead to the code returning within days.

fixSteps.title: Remove panel
fixSteps.instruction: Take off the rear evaporator cover.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fan motor and verify defrost heater/thermistor operation.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the code returns after replacing the fan motor.

faq.a: If the freezer has warmed above -6°F for over 4 hours, discard perishable items.

title: Freezer Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment thermistor is reading out of range.
fullDescription:
F1 indicates a problem with the freezer compartment temperature sensor (thermistor). The control board expects a resistance within a specific range; a short or open reading triggers F1.

Physical causes include a damaged thermistor, a pinched wire, or corrosion on the connector after defrost cycles. Sometimes a simple harness reseat clears the issue.

Replacement thermistors are inexpensive and installation is straightforward once the rear freezer panel is removed.

fixSteps.title: Find thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel to locate the sensor clipped near the evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure thermistor; compare to LG chart (e.g., ~16kΩ at 0°F).

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip old sensor, plug in new one, and remount.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor tests good but the code persists — likely a board issue.

faq.q: Can I keep the freezer running with F1?
faq.a: Yes, but temperature regulation will be unreliable; fix soon.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil temperature sensor is faulty.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the evaporator coil thermistor, used to time the defrost cycle, is out of range. When the sensor fails, defrost cycles become unreliable and frost can accumulate.

This thermistor is clipped to the evaporator and exposed to repeated freeze-thaw cycles, which shortens its life compared to the cabinet thermistor. Replacement is inexpensive.

If left unresolved, F2 often leads to a follow-on dH or Er DH error as the defrost cycle mistimes.

fixSteps.title: Locate thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Find the small clipped sensor on the evaporator fins.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in the new thermistor and re-clip.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if defrost issues persist after sensor replacement.

faq.a: Indirectly — it disrupts defrost timing which leads to frost and poor airflow.
Clipped to the evaporator fins behind the rear freezer panel.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Communication failure between main PCB and display/user interface board.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates a loss of communication between the main control board and the display or UI board. The two boards typically exchange data over a serial line; a broken wire, loose connector, or failed board causes E6.

After a power surge or moisture event, this is frequently the first code to appear. Reseating connectors sometimes clears it, but persistent E6 typically requires a board replacement.

Diagnosis requires access to both the display panel (front) and main control board (usually rear bottom).

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes then plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Access display and main board, unplug and firmly reseat ribbon cables.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for damage
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burned traces, swollen capacitors, or corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the suspect board (display first, then main) if reseating didn't help.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the main board is damaged; it requires programming on some models.

faq.a: The freezer may still cool but you won't be able to adjust settings.
Yes, especially after an E6 caused by a power event.

title: Ice Maker Fan Fault
shortDescription: The ice maker fan motor is not operating correctly.
fullDescription:
The IF error on LG freezers with ice makers indicates the ice maker compartment fan is not running at the expected RPM. This fan circulates cold air through the ice maker cavity to speed freezing.

Common causes include ice buildup, a failed fan motor, or a disconnected harness. The ice maker will slow or stop producing ice while the error is active, but the main freezer usually continues working normally.

Access is typically via the ice maker module or a small access panel inside the freezer door or compartment.

fixSteps.title: Remove ice bin
fixSteps.instruction: Empty and remove the ice storage bin.

fixSteps.title: Access fan
fixSteps.instruction: Open ice maker housing or door access panel to expose the fan.

fixSteps.title: Clear or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Defrost any ice and test fan motor; replace if it fails to spin freely.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the ice maker module is integrated and difficult to service.

faq.q: Will the main freezer still work?
faq.a: Yes, only ice making is affected by IF.

faq.q: How do I prevent ice in the fan area?
faq.a: Keep the ice bin properly seated and don't overfill to allow airflow.
